summary_paragraph: A man with a complex medical history including non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, COPD, insulin-dependent diabetes, and polysubstance use was admitted after being found unconscious following a fall. Initial imaging revealed a left subarachnoid hemorrhage and a skull fracture. His condition declined rapidly with a large intraparenchymal hemorrhage and 11 mm midline shift, leading to a decision against surgical intervention due to poor prognosis. He remained intubated and developed complications including pneumonia, acute kidney injury, hypernatremia, and hypotension. Despite supportive care, there was no neurological improvement. After a family meeting, the decision was made to transition to comfort measures only. He was terminally extubated and passed away on the final day of admission.
problems: Traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage without loss of consciousness, initial encounter
Hemiplegia, unspecified affecting right dominant side
Other fracture of base of skull, initial encounter
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
